text:
emily: Heads-up: we're changing the release cadence and freeze policy effective Mon 2026-03-30. Major trains -> every 2 weeks; minor/patch -> weekly. Purpose: fewer mid-week rollouts and more stable canaries.

chen: Will canary lengths change? Our embeddings jobs expect short canaries.

emily: Yes. New defaults: major=120m, minor/patch=45m, emergency hotpatch=30m (unchanged).

rahul: Behavior on failures? If a canary fails late in the window do we auto-revert? Oncall needs specifics.

emily: Auto-fallback rule: if error rate >=75% sustained for 5m, traffic flips back to previous variant automatically. That is a fallback. Full rollback requires deploy-owner approval unless the deploy sets auto-rollback:true.

deploy-bot: notice: canary_defaults updated -> {major:120m, minor:45m, hotpatch:30m} effective 2026-03-30T09:00:00Z

jen: Security-only fixes - can they bypass the major freeze?

emily: Security patches are exempt but must pass the security gating checklist and follow canary/fallback rules. Use the release-exemptions form for approval.

samir: I'll update the runbook, release checklist, and customer comms draft. Ping me for wording if you want a Dedicated partner blurb.

chen: Can someone add a copy-paste canary snippet to the runbook? Saves time.

emily: Will add this example to the runbook:

```json
{"release_type":"major","canary_duration":"120m","fallback_threshold":0.75,"fallback_window_mins":5,"rollback":"manual unless auto-rollback flag"}
```

rahul: I'll run a hotpatch drill next Wed to validate emergency flow and share results.

emily: Thanks. If you spot any gaps reply here or DM. We'll do a retrospective after the first biweekly major. :party_popper:
